*Summarise taxonomic composition across habitats and months using stacked barplots.*

### Define the barplot function

The function below identifies the most abundant taxa across the selected samples, calculates their mean relative abundance for each habitat and month, and displays the results as stacked barplots.

```r
plot_barplots <- function(rank, size_taxa = -1, top_x = 10) {
  mycols <- colorRampPalette(c(
    "#a6cee3", "#1f78b4", "#b2df8a", "#33a02c",
    "#fb9a99", "#e31a1c", "#fdbf6f", "#ff7f00",
    "#cab2d6", "#6a3d9a", "#ffff99", "#b15928"
  ))

  habitats <- names(habitat_cols)
  n_hab <- length(habitats)

  # ok is the same set of taxa in every panel, so we use one shared legend
  # in its own column, spanning the full figure height for readability
  layout(matrix(c(seq_len(n_hab), rep(n_hab + 1, n_hab)), nrow = n_hab),
         widths = c(4, 1.3))
  par(mar = c(2, 3, 2, 1))

  # Select the most abundant taxa across the samples retained in step 3
  ok <- sort(
    Matrix::rowMeans(cladecounts$norm[[rank]][, ix]),
    index.return = TRUE,
    decreasing = TRUE
  )$ix[1:top_x]

  if (size_taxa == -1) {
    size_taxa <- 2
  }

  for (hab in habitats) {
    ix_hab <- intersect(ix, which(habitat == hab))

    monthly_averages_matr <- matrix(
      ncol = 12,
      nrow = nrow(cladecounts$norm[[rank]])
    )

    for (j in 1:12) {
      ix2 <- intersect(ix_hab, which(month == j))

      if (length(ix2) > 1) {
        monthly_averages_matr[, j] <-
          Matrix::rowMeans(cladecounts$norm[[rank]][, ix2])
      }

      if (length(ix2) == 1) {
        monthly_averages_matr[, j] <-
          cladecounts$norm[[rank]][, ix2]
      }

      if (length(ix2) == 0) {
        monthly_averages_matr[, j] <- NA
      }
    }

    barplot(
      monthly_averages_matr[ok, ],
      col = mycols(length(ok)),
      main = hab
    )
  }

  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot.new()
  legend(
    "center",
    bty = "n",
    pch = 19,
    col = mycols(length(ok))[length(ok):1],
    cex = size_taxa,
    legend = rownames(cladecounts$norm[[rank]])[rev(ok)]
  )
}
```

The same paired sample set selected in [step 3](tutorial-03-map.qmd), stored in `ix`, is used both to select the most abundant taxa and to calculate the habitat-by-month averages.

### Choose a taxonomic rank

`sum_by_clade()` stores abundance tables at several taxonomic ranks. The numeric rank codes are:

1. kingdom (or domain)
2. phylum
3. class
4. order
5. family
6. genus
7. species

### Example: plot top orders

Plot the eight most abundant orders across habitats and months:

```r
plot_barplots(rank = 4, top_x = 8)
```
